title: NALSA & DLSA Free Legal Aid & Advice
target_audience: Women, children, SC/ST individuals, low-income citizens, industrial workmen, and persons in custody.
benefits: 100% free legal representation, free advocate assignment, court fee waiver, and preparation of appeals/petitions under Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 (Section 12).
eligibility: Women, children, SC/ST, custody undertrials, or individuals with annual income below prescribed limit (generally ₹3 Lakh).
documents_needed: Aadhaar Card, Income certificate / self-declaration, Case-related documents.
how_to_apply: Visit District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) at District Court, Front Office at High Court, or call national toll-free helpline 15100.

title: National Consumer Helpline (NCH) & e-Daakhil Consumer Complaint
target_audience: Consumers facing defective products, deficient services, overcharging, or refusal of refunds.
benefits: Free consumer dispute mediation through National Consumer Helpline and online filing of consumer cases at District, State, and National Consumer Commissions without mandatory advocate.
eligibility: Any consumer who purchased goods or hired services for personal use.
documents_needed: Bill/Invoice, warranty card, payment receipt, correspondence with seller.
how_to_apply: Call toll-free 1915, register grievance on consumerhelpline.gov.in, WhatsApp to 8800001915, or file formal case via edaakhil.nic.in.

title: Tenant Rights & Protection Against Unlawful Eviction
target_audience: Tenants and landlords residing in rented residential or commercial properties.
benefits: Rights to written rent agreement, essential services (water, electricity cannot be cut arbitrarily), reasonable notice period before eviction (usually 1-3 months), and security deposit refund.
eligibility: Lawful tenants with valid tenancy agreements under state Rent Control / Tenancy Acts.
documents_needed: Signed Rent Agreement, Rent receipts, Bank transfer records, Electricity/Water bill copies.
how_to_apply: Always insist on a registered or notarized rent agreement. In case of illegal harassment, file complaint with Rent Authority / Civil Court or local police.

title: Labor Rights: Minimum Wages, Working Hours & Gratuity
target_audience: Factory workers, daily wage laborers, construction workers, and contract staff.
benefits: Entitlement to statutory state Minimum Wages, 8-hour daily work limit, double wage rate for overtime, and Payment of Gratuity after 5 continuous years of service.
eligibility: All wage earners, contractual laborers, and industrial workmen.
documents_needed: Wage slips, Attendance card, Bank statement, ID badge.
how_to_apply: File grievance with District Labor Officer, Assistant Labor Commissioner (ALC), or Samadhan Portal at samadhan.labour.gov.in.

title: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act (PWDVA) & 181
target_audience: Women experiencing physical, verbal, emotional, or economic abuse in domestic relationships.
benefits: Right to reside in shared household, protection orders restraining abuser, monthly maintenance, medical expenses, child custody, and free legal aid/shelter home.
eligibility: Any woman living in a domestic relationship facing harassment or violence.
documents_needed: Medical report (if physical harm), Identity card, Marriage certificate (if available).
how_to_apply: Dial 181 (Women Helpline) or 112, or approach Protection Officer (PO) at District Magistrate / Women & Child Development office.

title: Right to Information (RTI) Act Basics & Online Filing
target_audience: Citizens seeking transparency on government projects, funds, tender decisions, and delayed files.
benefits: Statutory right to receive certified government documents, inspection of works, and status of applications within 30 days (48 hours in life/liberty matters). Fee is only ₹10 (free for BPL).
documents_needed: RTI Application letter, ₹10 Court fee stamp / IPO / Online fee receipt, BPL card (if seeking fee exemption).
how_to_apply: Submit physical application to Public Information Officer (PIO) of respective department or file online at rtionline.gov.in for central ministries.

title: National Lok Adalat for Fast, Fee-Free Mutual Settlement
target_audience: Parties with pending court cases or pre-litigation disputes (traffic challans, bank loans, electricity bills, matrimonial matters).
benefits: Zero court fees (refunded if already paid), final non-appealable amicable award, saves years of court visits, and promotes mutual cordial settlement.
eligibility: Both parties agreeing to explore compromise on compoundable matters.
documents_needed: Case number, summons copy, settlement proposal.
how_to_apply: Approach District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) secretary before the scheduled National Lok Adalat date.

title: Filing Police FIR, Zero FIR & Rights Upon Arrest
target_audience: Victims of cognizable crimes and citizens interacting with police stations.
benefits: Right to file 'Zero FIR' at ANY police station regardless of jurisdiction, free copy of FIR immediately, right to inform family member within 12 hours of arrest, and medical checkup.
eligibility: Victim or complainant reporting a cognizable offense (theft, assault, cyber fraud, missing person).
documents_needed: Written complaint detailing date, time, location, suspects, and eyewitnesses.
how_to_apply: Visit police station; if SHO refuses, send complaint to Superintendent of Police (SP) via registered post or file online e-FIR if state provides portal.

title: Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act
target_audience: Parents and senior citizens (aged 60+) unable to maintain themselves.
benefits: Legal entitlement to monthly maintenance (up to ₹10,000+) from adult children/heirs, protection against eviction from own house, and revocation of gifted property if neglected.
eligibility: Senior citizens and parents (biological, adoptive, or step-parents).
documents_needed: Age proof (Aadhaar/Voter ID), Proof of neglect/non-maintenance, Property papers (if applicable).
how_to_apply: File summary application before Maintenance Tribunal presided by Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM). No lawyer needed.

title: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (MACT) & Hit-and-Run Compensation
target_audience: Road accident victims, injured passengers, and legal heirs of deceased victims.
benefits: Compensation for medical treatment, loss of earning capacity, and death. Special statutory Solatium Fund gives ₹2,00,000 for death and ₹50,000 for grievous injury in hit-and-run cases.
eligibility: Victims or legal heirs of road motor accidents.
documents_needed: FIR copy, Detailed Accident Report (DAR), Medical bills, Post-mortem report (if death), Income proof.
how_to_apply: File claim petition before MACT at the place of accident or where victim resides, or apply for Hit-and-Run compensation via District Magistrate/SDM.
